messages:
Jordan (AcmeApp): Hey team — we're getting spikes of 429s since last deploy. Started ~10:02am UTC. App shows rate limit exceeded even though org quota remaining. Repro: client makes concurrent requests from a few IPs through our proxy. We use two API keys (mobile and server). Any ideas?
Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste response headers from a 429? Also, which API key used in the failing requests?
Jordan (AcmeApp): Header snippet from one 429:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 120/60
x-rw-quota-org: 950000/1000000
x-rw-quota-project: 20000/20000
x-rw-quota-key: 0/50000
x-rw-request-id: req_0a1b2c
```
We were using the mobile API key (meant for client side). mobile key is shared across multiple app instances, and our proxy sometimes rewrites Authorization (long story).
Alex (SRE): Interesting — that header combo suggests the org has headroom but the project-level quota is exhausted and key-level quota shows zero usage allowed? x-rw-quota-key: 0/50000 looks like a per-key enforcement set to 0 capacity (maybe revoked or scoped). Do you have any recent key rotation or a denylist policy? :mag_right: 
Jordan (AcmeApp): No rotation. We did replace the IP passthrough last week; upstream proxy adds X-Forwarded-For and rewrites Auth to a service key for some endpoints. Could that mix scoping?
Maya (Support): It can. If requests alternate between two Authorization values (mobile key and service key) but originate from same IP, the rate limiter might apply IP-based limits too depending on policy. Can you run a quick curl reproducer that hits /v1/generate and include both headers? Example we recommend:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <MOBILE_KEY>" \
  -H "X-Project: mobile" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Then repeat concurrently from two IPs.
Jordan (AcmeApp): I did that and see mixing: sometimes the response shows x-rw-rate-limit from IP tier: `ip: 100/10`. Other times project-level. It's non-deterministic.
Priya (Eng): This smells like a race in our rate-limit routing: requests hashed by (auth | ip | org) based on available identity. If the proxy strips auth for some calls the system falls back to IP scoping which is much stricter. We'll need logs. Maya — can you get Jordan to share a few raw request logs (headers + timestamp + request-id)? We'll escalate to runtime. :arrow_up: 
Jordan (AcmeApp): Sharing a sample with request-ids: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d, req_0a1b2e. Attached are logs (pasted below):
```
[10:02:13] req_0a1b2c - ip=34.210.11.9 auth=mobile_key header_X-Project=mobile path=/v1/generate
[10:02:13] req_0a1b2d - ip=34.210.11.9 auth=service_key header_X-Project=server path=/v1/generate
[10:02:13] req_0a1b2e - ip=34.210.11.12 auth=mobile_key header_X-Project=mobile path=/v1/generate
```
Maya (Support): Got it — thanks. Alex/Priya, two quick asks: 1) check whether rate-limiter falls back to IP scoping when auth missing/rewritten; 2) check a recent deploy yesterday that touched header parsing.
Alex (SRE): On it. Looking at runtime metrics now — I see a spike at 10:02 and a deploy at 09:58 that included proxy header normalization. There is a bug where Authorization header is normalized to lowercase in routing and our identity lookup is case-sensitive. So sometimes auth lookup fails and we map to IP scope. Ticketing this.
rate-limit-bot: Alert: 2026-03-15T10:02:13Z high-ip-throttle 34.210.11.9 hit threshold 120/s fallback_to_ip_scope=true
Priya (Eng): Thanks for the pointer, Alex. Proposed mitigation: add a server-side rule to prefer auth-derived identity if both auth and ip present; patch header normalization ASAP. Also suggest Jordan rotate the mobile key to a new key that is flagged client-only and set per-key quotas to avoid cross-project bleed.
Jordan (AcmeApp): Appreciate the plan. One more: how do billing and quota appear for org vs project? Billing bot earlier showed org usage within limits; but we were still throttled.
Maya (Support): Billing shows org tokens consumed across all projects. Rate limiting can be enforced at multiple levels (org, project, key, ip). You can have org billing not exhausted but be blocked by a stricter project or key-level quota. We'll loop in Billing if needed but sounds like enforcement not billing.
Jordan (AcmeApp): Ok, thanks. Please escalate to runtime and let me know ETA — this is impacting mobile users. :grimacing: 
Alex (SRE): Escalation created: RG-7289. Assigning to eng-runtime. ETA for patch: 4 hours to rollback header normalization, hotfix 1-2 hours after approval. Will monitor the request-ids you provided.
Maya (Support): Jordan — I'll keep this thread updated. If you can provide a short window with traffic when we can test fixes, ping here. :thumbsup:
